title: The Errand
summary: Carrie frames one simple municipal errand; Bjorn and Gunnar treat the objects as campaign equipment.

panelPlan.action: Bushwick kitchen morning. DTI folder, appointment slip, MetroCard, keys, Sharpie, banana, cold coffee. Carrie briefs Bjorn and Gunnar; Kin remain background.
Bjorn studies the MetroCard without touching it.
Carrie holds up the MetroCard.
Gunnar studies the numbered address on the appointment slip.
Bjorn looks from the card to the apartment door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: One errand. That is the whole day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: This is too thin to be tribute.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: It gets us on the train.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The city names its doors with numbers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: A summons that fears its own name.

title: Rules for Outside
summary: Carrie establishes public-behavior rules; Bjorn immediately searches for jurisdictional edges.

panelPlan.action: Carrie points at Bjorn and Gunnar, DTI folder under arm.
Carrie counts on fingers.
Bjorn takes the rule seriously.
Carrie continues without slowing down.
Bjorn considers the list.
Carrie opens the apartment door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: No threatening commuters. No touching phones. No challenging children.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: No declaring ownership over stairs, doors, benches, platforms, sidewalks, pigeons, or airspace.

title: Burial Road
summary: The subway entrance is the first threshold; Gunnar chooses observation over refusal.

panelPlan.action: Bushwick street and subway stairs. Carrie descends; Bjorn and Gunnar stop at the top.
Carrie looks back from halfway down.
Bjorn stares underground.
Gunnar watches commuters continuously descend.
Gunnar starts down the stairs, choosing the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: You did not say burial road.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: The Gate Refuses Her
summary: Carrie's confident demonstration fails at the turnstile, creating the first system puzzle.

panelPlan.action: Turnstile bank. Carrie holds the MetroCard ready while Bjorn and Gunnar observe.
Display reads PLEASE SWIPE AGAIN.
Carrie swipes again; another error beep.
A commuter behind them barely looks up.
Bjorn steps close to the locked turnstile and studies its steel bars with the same grave attention he would give a person blocking passage.
Carrie grips the MetroCard too tightly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: The iron is old and badly maintained.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Gunnar Reads the Swipe
summary: Gunnar studies repeated commuter behavior and solves the turnstile by pattern recognition.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar POV: hands swipe cards, tap phones, push bars; rhythm and angle repeat.
Gunnar tracks timing and pressure.
Carrie hands him the card.
Gunnar wipes the magnetic strip clean against his sleeve.
He swipes at the observed speed and angle. Green unlock.
Gunnar walks through; Carrie stares.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Since the gate respects you.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Many Paths
summary: Gunnar recognizes that passage has formal, informal, and forbidden routes.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar stands inside the gate and watches the whole turnstile bank.
A commuter taps a phone and passes.
Another commuter swipes a MetroCard.
Someone slips through an emergency gate behind another person.
A child ducks beneath the turnstile. Gunnar notices; Carrie notices Gunnar noticing.

title: Many Small Permissions
summary: Bjorn struggles with the gate while Gunnar names the real civic logic of the city.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn swipes too hard; error beep.
Bjorn swipes too slowly; error beep.
Carrie reaches around, swipes correctly and pushes him through with her hip.
Bjorn stands inside, dignified and offended.
Gunnar looks across cards, phones, signs, guards, gates and queues as one system.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: I was carried by another's victory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Everywhere we go, there's another yes you need: train, building, account, room.

title: The Iron Worm Screams
summary: A subway train roars into the station; Bjorn braces at the unfamiliar machine until Carrie identifies it and the doors open for ordinary commuters.

panelPlan.action: Platform. Carrie leads; Bjorn and Gunnar take in the underground space.
Headlights approach in the tunnel; rail rumble builds.
Train screams into station. Bjorn's hand reflexively closes around the Sharpie in his pocket, not a weapon.
Carrie catches his wrist before the gesture escalates.
Bjorn stares at the train, awed and alarmed but motionless.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: The iron worm screams before battle.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Crowd Without Banners
summary: Bjorn misreads commuter flow as a disorderly charge; New Yorkers simply route around him.

panelPlan.action: Doors open and commuters flood out.
Bjorn plants himself protectively in front of Carrie and Gunnar.
Carrie pulls his sleeve while commuters split around them.
Crowd continues without acknowledging Bjorn.
A commuter brushes Gunnar's shoulder without looking.
Bjorn turns; Carrie blocks him with the folder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: In New York, that's legally a greeting.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Mourner of the Worm
summary: A subway busker turns Bjorn's solemnity into warmth instead of ridicule.

panelPlan.action: A saxophonist plays by a tiled column, open case at his feet.
Bjorn turns toward the music, genuinely moved.
Carrie notices the open instrument case.
Bjorn approaches with hand over heart.
Carrie drops a dollar. The busker nods without surprise.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Portrait Mode
summary: Silas appears as attention-economy pressure, carrying prior neighbor history rather than reintroducing himself.

panelPlan.action: Silas is half-hidden behind a platform pillar, phone raised vertically.
Gunnar recognizes him without warmth.
Carrie turns, instantly dead-eyed.
Silas lowers the phone a little.
Carrie points at the phone.
Bjorn notices Silas.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Black Mirror
summary: Carrie prevents Silas from turning Gunnar's language into content; Silas backs off.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar studies Silas's phone from a respectful distance.
Silas brightens at the phrase.
Carrie steps toward him.
Bjorn calmly addresses Silas.
Silas pockets the phone; Carrie holds his eye.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: If your mirror steals from us, I will open it and free what is trapped inside.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Original Original
summary: On the train, Carrie fights a DTI records problem while the Vikings are physically compressed into modern public space.

panelPlan.action: Packed train. Bjorn rigid by a pole; Gunnar balances naturally; Carrie protects the bent DTI folder.
Carrie's phone rings: DTI TEMPORAL HOUSING / RECORDS.
Carrie answers.
Packet stamp: ORIGINAL COPY — DO NOT DUPLICATE EXCEPT FOR ORIGINAL PURPOSES.
Carrie stares into middle distance.
Carrie listens, visibly dying inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: DTI Voice
dialogueInline.text: Do you have the original original?

dialogueInline.speaker: DTI Voice
dialogueInline.text: Right. But is it the original copy, or the copy of the original?

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Everyone Carries a Gate
summary: Gunnar connects transit access to the larger structure of modern civic identity.

panelPlan.action: Across the car, a man spreads cream cheese with a plastic knife.
Bjorn watches with concern.
Carrie covers the phone.
Gunnar watches phones, badges, cards, earbuds, delivery bags and notification screens.
Gunnar's insight lands quietly, not as a gag.
Carrie hears him and briefly stops fighting the call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: He butchers bread with a child's blade.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: The City Left Scars
summary: A moved DTI annex creates a navigation problem; Gunnar reads overwritten signage as physical history.

panelPlan.action: Transfer station. Carrie stops in pedestrian flow, still on phone.
Layered overhead signs and service-change paper cover older arrows.
Carrie flatly answers.
Gunnar takes the appointment slip and studies the layered wayfinding.
Tape residue and an older arrow remain visible under a newer notice.
Gunnar points to a passage Carrie had ignored.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Can the function sign a form?

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The city changed its mind but left scars.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: Without Blood or Shame
summary: Gunnar's route is correct, and Bjorn demonstrates learned turnstile competence.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar leads Carrie and Bjorn through the transfer passage against a cross-current of commuters.
They reach the final exit turnstile.
Bjorn holds the MetroCard with deliberate restraint.
Bjorn swipes correctly. Green unlock, clean click.
Bjorn exits, pleased but contained.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: I defeated the gate without blood or shame.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: That is the dream of public transit.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: The House Hides Its Name
summary: The destination itself is bureaucratically illegible, reinforcing that Carrie can know the system and still be failed by it.

panelPlan.action: Exterior municipal building: plain, underfunded, many bad budget cycles.
One sign reads DEPARTMENT OF TEMPORAL INTEGRATION.
Another sign reads MUNICIPAL HISTORIC DISPLACEMENT SERVICES.
A third reads OFFICE OF UNSCHEDULED PERSONS — ANNEX B.
Carrie stands under all three signs; Bjorn studies them as conflicting heraldry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: This house hides its true name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: This house lost a budget meeting.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: The Closed Side Entrance
summary: Posted instructions contradict each other; Gunnar begins reading the building as he read the subway.

panelPlan.action: Taped notice: TEMPORARILY MOVED — USE SIDE ENTRANCE.
Directly below: SIDE ENTRANCE CLOSED.
Carrie tries the locked side door anyway. It does not move.
Gunnar scans front doors, security desk, alley, delivery entrance and service door rather than staring at the sign.
Bjorn waits for Gunnar's judgment instead of taking the door as a challenge.
Gunnar watches a maintenance worker wheel trash toward the service alley.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The one no one bothered to name.

source: Enhanced from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2, current Master Project Bible, and released Issue 1 canon

title: The Rat Path
summary: Carrie insists on the official entrance while Gunnar follows the building's actual traffic and identifies a working service path.

panelPlan.action: Continue directly from Page 18. A maintenance worker wheels trash toward the service alley while Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar stand beside the contradictory SIDE ENTRANCE notices; Carrie still carries the bent DTI folder.
Carrie steps between Gunnar and the alley, trying to preserve one last boundary between navigation and trespass.
The worker badges an unmarked service door and drags the bin through. Gunnar watches the sequence instead of the sign.
Carrie points back toward the locked official entrance. Bjorn studies the unmarked door with Gunnar, trusting Gunnar's judgment instead of treating the building as a challenge.
Gunnar notes deliveries, staff traffic and the delayed door closer: a working route the building never labels for the public.
Another employee approaches the same service door with coffee. Gunnar looks to Carrie with complete seriousness; Carrie knows the question before he asks it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: We are not sneaking into a city office.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Then why does the city keep an entrance for people carrying trash?

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: It is a gate that opens.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: A gate that opens is information.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: I hate that you know to ask this now.

source: Recovered from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2 and enhanced to the locked 24-page Issue 3 ending in the current Master Project Bible.

title: The Hidden Hall
summary: The working service door opens; Gunnar chooses the route, forcing Carrie to follow while Bjorn recognizes the unseen infrastructure behind the bureaucracy.

panelPlan.location: DTI service entrance and interior service corridor
panelPlan.action: A DTI employee slips through the service door carrying coffees and a box labeled ARCHIVAL DONUTS — DO NOT DATE-STAMP.

panelPlan.location: DTI service entrance and interior service corridor
panelPlan.action: Gunnar sees the opening; Carrie sees Gunnar see it.

panelPlan.location: DTI service entrance and interior service corridor
panelPlan.action: Gunnar catches the door before it closes without forcing anything and states the practical objective back to Carrie.

panelPlan.location: DTI service entrance and interior service corridor
panelPlan.action: Bjorn follows Gunnar. Carrie hurries after them with the bent folder, arguing while keeping the group together.

panelPlan.location: DTI service entrance and interior service corridor
panelPlan.action: Gunnar holds the service door for Carrie and the employee rather than charging ahead. Carrie crosses because losing them inside is worse.
Interior service corridor: fluorescent tubes, folding chairs, toner boxes, broken copier, exposed conduit and mismatched municipal arrows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: You said we had to reach the office.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: I did not say through the employee entrance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Your city has hidden roads for those who keep it alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: My city has fire codes and people who will call security.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Then we should not block the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: We have entered the hidden hall.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: We are calling it a hallway.

title: The Building Left Scars
summary: Conflicting room numbers stall Carrie, but Gunnar reads staff movement and physical traces to identify the current path through the annex.

panelPlan.action: Carrie catches a passing DTI staffer while Gunnar studies layered arrows and old room labels. Carrie names the task precisely.
The staffer points toward 2A. Carrie immediately sees a newer sign saying 2A NOW 4C.
Another notice reads 4C TEMPORARILY 2A. The staffer clarifies without treating it as unusual; Bjorn interprets the room-number conflict as territorial absurdity.
Carrie tells Bjorn to stay with the literal problem while Gunnar notices the coffee employee from Page 20 has vanished around a turn marked by worn yellow floor tape, wheel scuffs and staff traffic.
Carrie challenges Gunnar's method. Gunnar points out that staff behavior is the most current map available.
The DTI staffer points to the same yellow tape. A small reception placard is visible at the far end. Carrie has to accept Gunnar read it correctly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Reception. We need Temporal Housing Confirmation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: Please do not encourage the rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Which way did the coffee go?

dialogueInline.speaker: DTI Staff
dialogueInline.text: He's right. Follow the yellow tape to reception.

title: The Rat Path Also Has a Gate
summary: Reaching reception does not end the permissions problem; Bjorn confronts another ritualized form while Gunnar recognizes that even the unofficial route terminates in procedure.

panelPlan.action: Reception table beneath WELCOME HISTORICALLY DISPLACED INDIVIDUALS — PLEASE DO NOT ALTER THE PAST WHILE WAITING. Other clients wait with ordinary municipal fatigue.
The receptionist looks up, unimpressed, and slides a clipboard across laminate without asking how they entered.
Bjorn and Gunnar stare at the clipboard. Bjorn frames the signature as an oath; Gunnar sees their discovered route still ends at a formal permission point.
Bjorn reaches for the pen with grave ritual precision. Carrie intercepts the grip before it resembles a dagger hold; the receptionist supplies the real concern.
The blue pen chained to the desk pulls taut as Bjorn signs. He lifts the pen and chain to eye level; the receptionist points at the desk fitting and answers without looking surprised.
Carrie watches Bjorn finish while Gunnar studies signs: TEMPORAL HOUSING CONFIRMATION — ROOM 2A / 2A NOW 4C / 4C TEMPORARILY 2A.

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: The rat path also has a gate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Why is the pen chained if you trust the oath?

source: Recovered from THE IRON WORM 20-page draft v2 and enhanced to the locked 24-page Issue 3 ending in the current Master Project Bible.

title: The Errand
summary: Carrie gets the housing confirmation stamped and then hands Gunnar the route home instead of leading him back.

panelPlan.action: Carrie puts the bent DTI folder and disputed document on the counter with controlled finality: the earlier phone-call phrase is now a physical problem she intends to end.
The receptionist checks the paper and calmly calls it the original copy. Carrie makes them distinguish the exact phrase she was told on the train.
The receptionist points to the tiny ORIGINAL mark already on the page. Carrie absorbs that the detour was vocabulary, not missing evidence.

panelPlan.location: DTI service counter and receptionist desk
panelPlan.action: Bjorn asks whether the process is satisfied. The receptionist stamps the confirmation with an ordinary heavy desk stamp: THUNK.

panelPlan.location: DTI service counter and receptionist desk
panelPlan.action: Gunnar watches the stamp and identifies the true endpoint: all the doors and signs led to this authorization. Carrie corrects the abstraction with exhausted satisfaction.
Outside reception, Carrie stops instead of taking the lead. She hands Gunnar the MetroCard and keeps the completed folder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Receptionist
dialogueInline.text: Then she meant the copy marked original.

dialogueInline.speaker: Carrie
dialogueInline.text: That distinction cost me forty minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Bjorn
dialogueInline.text: Can the oath now be honored?

dialogueInline.speaker: Gunnar
dialogueInline.text: Then this was the true gate.
